text: Tiring-house exchange after the summer closure vote

speaker: John Heminges
text: Three dates at the foot of the sheet and not one figure written under them. Saturday the twenty-sixth, Monday the twenty-fifth of August, and Thursday the seventeenth to look again.

speaker: Augustine Phillips
text: Will Kemp took his coat out the door still muttering about Kent. He meant every word of his against.

speaker: William Shakespeare
text: He has a right to it. Five shillings in a country town against ten in Shoreditch is an easy sum for a sharer and a hard one for a hired man.

speaker: John Heminges
text: Oats are dearer every mile and country mayors want no crowd at their gate. A wagon eats coin on wet days and dry days alike. An empty yard costs us nothing till we open it.

speaker: Augustine Phillips
text: I sat on the chest and kept my mouth shut because the argument was already finished. I saved my throat for tonight's singing.

speaker: William Shakespeare
text: Thomas made me own my share of the vote aloud. August suits the pages better than it suits the road, and I am not pretending otherwise.

speaker: John Heminges
text: The road stays a guess till the seventeenth. Lock the sheet in the desk, Augustine — we have Richard's twenty-seven years waiting at the Jackdaw.

speaker: William Shakespeare
text: I have his pearwood glass wrapped in cloth under my arm. Let us walk before the capon cools.
